## Simple explanation

Machine learning (ML) is a way to build software that learns patterns from
examples instead of relying only on rules written by a programmer. A trained
model can use those patterns to make predictions on new inputs.

## Technical explanation

An ML system uses data and an optimization procedure to select a model from a
family of possible functions. In supervised learning, it learns from input and
target pairs; in unsupervised learning, it finds structure without supplied
target labels. Reinforcement learning optimizes behavior using feedback from
actions and outcomes.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

ML is the foundation for systems such as classifiers, recommenders, language
models, and forecasting tools. Engineering a useful ML product involves more
than selecting an algorithm: data quality, evaluation, deployment, monitoring,
and feedback are also essential.

## How it works

1. Define a task and collect representative data.
2. Choose a model and an objective that reflect the task.
3. Train the model by adjusting its parameters to reduce the objective.
4. Evaluate it on data not used for fitting.
5. Deploy and monitor the model, then improve it as needs or data change.

## Practical example

A photo app can learn to classify images by training on examples paired with
labels such as "cat" and "dog." After training, it can predict labels for
previously unseen photos.

## Common misconceptions

- Machine learning is not synonymous with deep learning; deep learning is one family of ML methods.
- A model's training performance does not guarantee that it will work well on new data.
- ML systems learn from the data and objective they are given; they do not automatically learn the right goal.
